title: Hong Kong Companies Investing in AI Skills Training
paragraphs: Companies in Hong Kong are spending more time training their employees, and artificial intelligence (AI) has become their most important training area, according to a new survey.

The survey was carried out by the Hong Kong Institute of Human Resource Management (HKIHRM) between February and April 2026. It received responses from 127 companies in 18 industries, which together employ nearly 80,000 full-time workers.
The survey found that employees received an average of 19.4 hours of training in 2025. That was 6.8% more than in 2024, and the highest level since 2011.

For the first time, AI was rated as an important training area by more companies than any other subject. This was true for staff at all levels, including 61% of middle managers, 58% of senior managers and 54% of junior staff.

Companies are also becoming more open to the use of AI at work. About 82% now allow their employees to use generative AI tools, up from 73% in 2024. Meanwhile, the number of companies using AI learning tools in their training programs jumped from 16% to 40%.

However, many companies are still at an early stage. In a separate poll of 96 employers, only 29% said they had already added AI-assisted tools to their training. Another 14% plan to do so in 2026, and 24% by 2027, while 32% have no plans to do so.

Despite the focus on AI, companies have not forgotten about other skills. Problem-solving, communication and interpersonal skills remain among the top priorities, and leadership development is the most important training goal for 2026.

Charles Ho of the HKIHRM said that digital learning is not meant to replace face-to-face training. He also said that AI training is about helping employees learn new skills, not about reducing the number of workers. Another HKIHRM leader, Dr. Chester Tsang, said that future competitiveness is not only about technology, adding that training should also cover values such as integrity and responsibility.
